name: ValidateAppAuth
description: Internal authentication helper called by every HC6 app SP (and by the publicWeb_ wrappers, since a browser is a device). Resolves the calling device's credentials from HC.Device by @deviceId, then applies three checks in order, each its own errorType so the client can act differently: (1) device or user not found → errorCode 1300 + @spNumber, errorType 3; (2) the device was deliberately signed out (HC.Device.SignedOutAt IS NOT NULL, written only by hcapp_signOutDevice — E9.F7.S19) → 1200 + @spNumber, errorType 7, on which the client wipes the install; tested BEFORE the token so a rotated secret is not mistaken for a drifting clock; (3) HC.CHECK_ACCESS_TOKEN_V2(@userId, @procName, @accessToken, COALESCE(@param, @deviceSecret), @timeWindow) = 0 → 1100 + @spNumber, errorType 1, on which the client must NOT wipe. On success returns @userId (HC.Hasher.id), @deviceSecret and @timeWindow via OUTPUT parameters with @errorCode NULL; on failure populates the error OUTPUTs for the calling SP to emit its error rowset(s). NOT exposed as an API endpoint. Does not read Device.removed (300 devices carry removed = 1 and are in active use).

parameters.name: deviceId
parameters.description: Calling device UUID (HC.Device.id). Looked up to retrieve UserId, DeviceSecret, TimeWindow and SignedOutAt. No default: callers always pass it.

parameters.name: accessToken
parameters.description: Short-lived cryptographic token from the app. Validated via HC.CHECK_ACCESS_TOKEN_V2 using @userId, @procName, and the resolved token context string.

parameters.name: procName
parameters.description: Caller MUST pass OBJECT_NAME(@@PROCID). Baked into the token hash on the Flutter client side — must match the SP name exactly for validation to succeed.

parameters.name: spNumber
parameters.description: Two-digit SP number assigned to the calling SP. Used to compute errorCode: auth failure = 1100 + @spNumber, device not found = 1300 + @spNumber.

parameters.name: param
parameters.description: Optional compound context (e.g. deviceSecret + targetUserId / + scanData). When provided it REPLACES @deviceSecret as the token validation context string, binding the token to a target. Default NULL = standard device-secret-only auth.

parameters.name: userId
parameters.description: OUTPUT: HC.Hasher.id of the authenticated user (resolved via Device.UserId). NULL on failure.

parameters.name: deviceSecret
parameters.description: OUTPUT: HC.Device.DeviceSecret (stored uppercase). NULL on failure. Returned to calling SPs that need it to construct compound @param strings for nested SP calls.

parameters.name: timeWindow
parameters.description: OUTPUT: HC.Device.TimeWindow (seconds). Used by HC.CHECK_ACCESS_TOKEN_V2 for token expiry validation. NULL on failure.

parameters.name: errorCode
parameters.description: OUTPUT: NULL on success. 1300 + @spNumber device/user not found; 1200 + @spNumber device signed out; 1100 + @spNumber token invalid.

parameters.name: errorType
parameters.description: OUTPUT: NULL on success. 3 device not found; 7 signed out (client wipes the install); 1 token invalid (client must not wipe).

parameters.name: errorId
parameters.description: OUTPUT: NULL on success. HC.ErrorLog GUID written on any failure.

parameters.name: errorTitle
parameters.description: OUTPUT: NULL on success. 'Device not registered', 'Signed out' or 'Invalid access token'.

parameters.name: errorMsg
parameters.description: OUTPUT: NULL on success. User-facing error message on failure.

sideEffects: INSERT HC.ErrorLog on device-not-found (userId NULL), signed-out and token-invalid failures, HcVersion from HC6.DeviceHcVersion(@deviceId).
prerequisites: HC.Device row must exist for @deviceId with a non-null, non-zero UserId and SignedOutAt NULL for auth to pass.
HC.Device.SignedOutAt (added by db/hc6/app/archive/2026-09-20_device_signed_out.sql) is not in db/schema/tables/HC.Device.Table.sql — the schema snapshot is stale.
breakingChangeRules: Never change the OUTPUT parameter semantics — all callers read them by position after EXEC.
Never change the errorType integer codes (1 = auth, 3 = not found, 7 = signed out) without updating all callers — the app wipes the install on 7 and must never wipe on 1.
Never change the errorCode formula (1100+N / 1200+N / 1300+N) without updating all callers and the Flutter error handler.
Never change the token context string logic (COALESCE(@param, @deviceSecret)) without coordinating with Flutter.
Never add a new OUTPUT parameter without updating all callers — SQL EXEC with named params is safe but callers must add the new OUTPUT binding.

codeSmells.issue: SP body not wrapped in TRY/CATCH
codeSmells.detail: Lines 47-122 have no TRY/CATCH. Every caller invokes this BEFORE its own BEGIN TRY (that is the sanctioned placement), so a runtime error inside it — e.g. the HC.ErrorLog INSERT failing — is a raw, unlogged 500 for the whole call. Low likelihood, but it sits under every authenticated call in the product.

@deviceId, @accessToken, @procName and @spNumber (lines 2-5) have no SQL default. Only HC6 SPs call it with named parameters, so an omission is a developer error caught on first run rather than a client-facing unlogged 500.
